newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED BEAT BLACKBURN TO STAY TOP IN ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED BEAT BLACKBURN TO STAY TOP IN ENGLAND.

text.p: Manchester United bounced back from their midweek European Cup defeat at Borussia Dortmund to win 3-2 at Blackburn on Saturday to stay top of the English premier league.

Goals from Andy Cole (33rd minute), Paul Scholes (43rd) and their French skipper Eric Cantona (80th) secured the points for the impressive-looking champions after Cantona missed a 22nd-minute penalty with the scores at 0-0. Billy McKinlay scored for Rovers after 36 minutes and Paul Warhurst added a second two minutes from time.

The victory moved United on to 66 points with five matches to play and kept them three points ahead of Arsenal who beat Leicester 2-0 at Highbury with goals from Tony Adams (35th) and David Platt (66th).
Arsenal, who have four matches remaining, have 63 points, three more than Liverpool who play at Sunderland on Sunday.

Southampton moved out of the relegation zone with a 2-0 home win over fellow strugglers West Ham despite playing for half the match with 10 men following the 44th-minute dismissal of Jason Dodd for violent conduct.

Michael Evans and Eyal Berkovic scored for the Saints while Jim Magilton missed a first-half penalty. In the only other league games played on Saturday, Derby beat Aston Villa 2-1 and Everton eased their relegation fears with a 1-0 home win over Tottenham.
